problem: Two cars, $A$ and $B,$ are both initially at the point $O,$ and they both depart from $O$ at the same time. Car $A$ travels due east, and its distance from $O$ is given by $3t\,\text{ft}.$ Car $B$ travels due north, and its distance from $O$ is $2{t}^{2}\,\text{ft}.$ Here, $t$ is the time, measured in seconds. What is the rate of the change of the distance between the two cars after $2$ seconds?

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Related Rates Using the Pythagorean Theorem

feedback.problem: A drone is released vertically from the ground at a constant velocity of $40\text{ ft/s}.$ An observer stands $120\text{ ft}$ away from the launch point. What is the rate of change of the distance between the drone and the observer $4$ seconds after the drone was launched?
feedback.worked_solution:
We start by drawing a diagram of the problem.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14066033/assets/3f85af53794fa2f61a353f2e088cc1cecc9fc04f7453b97aa0ca808475e40035.png)

In the diagram,

- $x$ is the distance between the observer and the launch point,

- $y$ is the distance between the drone and the launch point, and

- $z$ is the distance between the observer and the drone.

As shown in the diagram, $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ form a right triangle with $z$ as the hypotenuse. We wish to find the rate of change of $z,$ which is $\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}.$

First, we determine the drone altitude after $4$ seconds. Since its velocity is constant, we get 

$$
y=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot t=40(4)=160\text{ ft}
$$

We can find $z$ using the Pythagorean Theorem, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ {120}^{2}+{160}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ 40\,000 & ={z}^{2} \\ z & =200\,\text{ft}\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that:

- $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=40\,\text{ft}/\text{s},$

- the distance between the observer and the launch pad remains the same, so $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=0.$

Finally, we differentiate both sides of ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}={z}^{2}$ with respect to $t$ and then substitute the known values, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({z}^{2}) \\ 2x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} \\ 2(120)(0)+2(160)(40) & =2(200)\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} \\ 12\,800 & =400\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} & =32\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the distance between the drone and the observer increases at a rate of $32\,\text{ft/s}$ after $4$ seconds.
